dedupe_keys.name: simpact smart irrigation for urban cooling bicentennial park sydney olympic park

description: This short communication reports the SIMPaCT project, Smart Irrigation Management for Parks and Cool Towns, which links soil-moisture forecasts to overnight irrigation set-points so that a large public park can give evaporative cooling in hot spells as well as save water. Researchers at Western Sydney University and partners built it with Sydney Olympic Park Authority and Sydney Water, funded by the NSW Digital Restart Fund. Coverage is the roughly 40 hectare Bicentennial Park, instrumented with 202 soil-moisture sensors, 50 temperature and humidity nodes and 13 weather stations, whose data feed a per-zone digital twin that writes proposals to the existing irrigation controller. Forecast errors are small, with a mean absolute error of 0.78 percent, and a mutual-information virtual sensor covers device failures. Format and access: an open CC BY 4.0 preprint and a companion paper, with a Zenodo data deposit of hourly soil moisture that could not be opened from the cloud. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the paper; free. Caveats: the paper does not measure cooling or water savings, and it covers one park. It supports climate adaptation and heat mitigation planning for irrigated green infrastructure. A related catalogue record is the NGIF sensor data.

name: SIMPaCT smart irrigation for urban cooling, Bicentennial Park, Sydney Olympic Park
outcomes: Per-sensor soil-moisture forecasts had a mean absolute error of 0.78 percent, and kNN beat SARIMA on upper-quartile error (0.71 versus 0.93); daily runs propose overnight irrigation set-points for operator review, with virtual sensors covering failed devices. Cooling and water savings were not quantified.
